title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：officer　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 officer 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the clerk ① followed the officer that no applicant in the office would have described, and he said the following was the whole of the month. The ② officer, meaning the leader itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed undescribed in the book; an officer, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ officer in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ officer at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An officer, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the clerk said the describing is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the officer was the whole of the matter, meaning the authority and not the leader. The ⑥ officer, meaning the authority and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; officer, he said, is either something you follow or the only word that means both a leader and an authority. He said the authority is the part they remember.

By 1987 the ⑦ officer had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ officer of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of describing; officer, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ officer I remember is the leader described in the file, which closed in 1989 and is still described as the quietest in the office. An ⑩ officer, my mother said in 1991, is the only leader that improves by being described; every officer, she said, is an authority that has agreed to look like a leader. She said the authority was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 军官；官员（指办事处里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 军官；官员（指那位军官本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：follow the officer 听命这一位军官
D. n. 军官；官员（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 军官之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的军官之事）
F. n. 军官；官员（指卷宗里写到、被描述的那一位）
G. n. 军官、威权（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 威权（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: followed the officer that no applicant in the office would have described

answers.why: follow the officer 意为“听命这一位军官”，1982 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯描述的一位军官做了一遍。
officer 意为“军官；官员”，指那位军官本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被描述。
officer 意为“军官；官员”，指办事处里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
officer 意为“军官；官员”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
officer 意为“军官、威权”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位威权就是那件事的全部。
officer 意为“威权”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位军官，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
officer 意为“军官；官员”，指卷宗里写到、被描述的那一位，到 1987 年这一位成了卷宗里的一行。
officer 意为“军官之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的军官之事是一处办事处和三个月份的描述。
officer 意为“军官；官员”，我记得的是卷宗里描述过的那一位，1989 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一位。
officer 为抽象总称，母亲 1991 年说，军官是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的军官。
